architectural_shifts: from pure conditional-variance Gaussian imputation (nRMSE 1.067 in search) to quantile-transformed wrapper-selected NNLS-stacked imputation (nRMSE 1.028)
adding a monotone latent-skill member and A-optimal selector to the stack gave identical search score to the stacked incumbent (no measurable gain)
final sealed evaluation nRMSE 0.562 overall, with MTEB error decreasing as k grows (0.787 at k=2 to 0.638 at k=20)
benchmarks: Open LLM Leaderboard (IFEval, BBH, MATH Lvl 5, GPQA, MUSR, MMLU-PRO)
reference_query_plan.central_topic: Choosing a small subset of k benchmarks to run on a new model and imputing its scores on the remaining benchmarks from a historical model-by-benchmark score matrix (MTEB, HELM Lite, Open LLM Leaderboard), evaluated by held-out-model normalized RMSE against random selection, ridge and permuted-control baselines.
comparators: greedy ridge regression on selected benchmarks
low-rank matrix completion / probabilistic matrix factorization
item-response-theory style latent ability models for LLM evaluation
observational scaling laws and Sloth skill scaling laws
core_methods: EM-estimated Gaussian covariance with conditional-mean imputation of missing scores
wrapper cross-validated forward selection of benchmarks
per-target NNLS stacked ensemble of imputers
monotone-link latent-skill model with Huber MAP and Laplace posterior

internal terms such as combined_score, rubric, program_1, eligible

queries.query: predicting language model benchmark performance from a subset of benchmarks low-rank
queries.rationale: Central problem: infer a new model's scores on unrun benchmarks from k observed ones using a historical score matrix.

queries.query: greedy subset selection conditional variance Gaussian process sensor placement submodular
queries.rationale: Theory-side literature behind greedy conditional-variance selection and its near-optimality guarantees.

queries.query: EM algorithm multivariate Gaussian missing data covariance estimation conditional mean imputation
queries.rationale: The incumbent imputer estimates a Gaussian covariance by EM from a partially observed matrix and imputes by conditional mean.

queries.query: stacked generalization non-negative least squares ensemble
queries.rationale: Per-target NNLS stack of imputers is the best-scoring configuration; need the stacking/NNLS-combining reference.

queries.query: matrix completion low-rank probabilistic matrix factorization missing entries
queries.rationale: Expected comparator family for score-matrix imputation with a low-rank/latent structure.

queries.query: item response theory efficient evaluation of language models few examples
queries.rationale: Latent-ability models (monotone-link latent skill) and benchmark-sparsification comparators such as metabench/tinyBenchmarks.

queries.query: observational scaling laws low-dimensional capability space language models
queries.rationale: Supports the low-dimensional latent skill explanation and the starter-list work on cross-benchmark predictability (including Sloth).

queries.query: A-optimal Bayesian experimental design active feature selection
queries.rationale: A-optimal latent selector was added in the third variant and gave no gain; need experimental-design background.

queries.query: cross-benchmark agreement of LLM benchmarks correlation of model rankings
queries.rationale: Variation in predictability across leaderboards and the permuted-control gap relate to benchmark-agreement analysis.

queries.query: MTEB massive text embedding benchmark leaderboard
queries.rationale: MTEB is the primary data source and the setting with the highest error across k.

result_driven_themes: few benchmarks recover the rest only modestly: skill over random selection is small (final 0.016) while gain over greedy ridge is larger (0.099)
prediction difficulty varies by leaderboard (HELM 0.50, Open LLM 0.48, MTEB 0.70)
diminishing returns in k on MTEB
permuted-control gap shows that cross-benchmark structure is real
low-rank / latent-skill structure in model-by-benchmark matrices
